$meta.name: Jarvis · v2
$meta.source: docs/design/v2/PROMPT.md and its boards (docs/design/v2/*.dc.html): the JARVIS v2 design language, 2026-11-08. It took over from the Build Brief (the Build Brief's boards, the same day), which replaced Reactor II (GLASS_HUD, c2-reactor.html); DECISIONS.md says why and how to undo each step.
$meta.format: W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) draft: groups of { "$type", "$value" } leaves; "{group.path}" is an alias; "{color.path@0.55}" is that colour at an alpha, resolved to rgba() — so a tint is Glass at an alpha and moves when Glass moves, never a second hex.
$meta.rule: This is the only file in the repository where a colour, size, radius, shadow or duration is typed by a human. Everything else is generated by design/build.py and checked by scripts/verify/token_lint.py. One value is derived rather than typed: spring.*.ratio (Compose's damping ratio) is computed by build.py from stiffness, damping and mass.
$meta.platforms: Groups named `android` are phone-only scales (sp, dp) and are not emitted to CSS; everything else is emitted everywhere. design/generated/console-theme.json is the terminal's reading of the same table.
$meta.naming: CSS custom property = --jv-<path>, with the shorthands the console already uses: color.* → --jv-*, type.family.* → --jv-font-*, type.size.* → --jv-fs-*, type.tracking.* → --jv-track-*, elevation.glow-* → --jv-glow-*, elevation.panel/float → --jv-elev-*, motion.dur.* → --jv-dur-*, motion.ease.* → --jv-ease-*, motion.stagger.* → --jv-stagger-*, motion.reactor.* → --jv-rx-*, chrome.* → --jv-*, material.* → --jv-material-*, depth.* → --jv-depth-*, spring.* → --jv-spring-*, light.* → --jv-light-*. The corner brackets are chrome.bracket (their arm) in color.accent; the brief draws them on every panel.

bg.$description: The ground under everything (v2: the Core2 board). Never flat: the core's radial glow (color.core-glow, then color.core.haze) is painted on it (chrome.stage-ground).

bg-raised.$description: The ground one step up: the middle stop of the core's radial glow, a region that should read as raised without becoming a panel.

panel.$description: A panel's colour. Panels draw it at 0.78 alpha (material.panel.solid) under a 1 px accent edge; this solid is the fallback where nothing can be translucent.

panel-solid.$description: The console's name for an opaque panel; same value as panel.

surface-2.$description: A raised control or row: a hovered rail button, an active segment. The accent at about 8 % over the panel, solid.

surface-sunken.$description: Inset: the command terminal, a diff, console output.

accent.$description: Cyan, the accent (brief §1): what is live now, the selected rail section, the corner brackets, the one filled control on a panel, the focus ring.

accent-deep.$description: Cyan at rest: the idle reactor's secondary rings, a secondary rule, a link at rest.

accent-lift.$description: Cyan lifted: a hovered link, the reactor's highlight arc, the reactor while speaking.

accent-ink.$description: Text on an accent fill. Never on the ground.

warn.$description: Amber (brief §1): warnings and needs-you — an approval, a clarifying question, a GPU near full, the offline ring.

warming.$description: warming: not ready yet, getting there — a model cold start, a reconnect in progress. A hotter amber than warn so a cold start and a held approval read apart.

danger.$description: Pink (brief §1): errors and security — a failed check, an unknown LAN device, the alert's pulsing edge.

danger-text.$description: Danger as body text, lifted to clear AA on the ground.

text.$description: Body text (v2: the main text, the Core2 board's #F2FBFF). text-bright has the same value since v2: projected light has one main grade, and hierarchy comes from size and the display face.

text-bright.$description: The one line to read first: the reply, the title, the figure (brief §1 text).

text-faint.$description: Labels (v2): the uppercase tracked captions, timestamps, units. About 9:1 on the ground, so it clears AA. For marks that are not text use tick.

tick.$description: Mark: not text — bezel ticks, dashed coils, decorative dots, an idle agent node. Below AA on purpose; nothing is read in it.

line.$description: A border you should notice: the accent at 14 % over the ground (the boards' panel edge), solid for the surfaces that cannot blend.

line-soft.$description: A divider: the accent at 10 % over the ground (the rail's edge, a panel header rule).

line-hair.$description: Between rows: the accent at 8 % over the ground (the boards' .row rule).

wash.$description: The accent as a tint: a selected rail button, a hovered row.

wash-strong.$description: The accent as a stronger tint: a pressed toggle, a lit room on the house plan.

glow.$description: The accent as light: the reactor's ring glow, the sweep line's halo, a lit agent node.

scrim.$description: The text scrim: Room at half, faded in over motion.dur.fast behind a panel's text blocks when the sampled backdrop is brighter than the halo (GLASS_HUD §3.2). A layer inside the panel, so the glass edge keeps its light; it never covers a control.

orb.$description: The reactor's fixed parts, which are not state colours: the bezel's substrate, the dark housing (the rings of the kill-switch state) and the hub. The per-state blob palettes that lived here fed the old orb; the state colour C is color.reactor.* now (GLASS_HUD §10).

housing.$description: Reactor housing: the dark rings of the kill-switch state; the inside of the reactor's bezel.

reactor.$description: The arc reactor's state colour C — the eleven states of GLASS_HUD §10, each an alias of a base colour so no hue is added. Listening, thinking and tool share Reactor light and are told apart by motion; idle and goal share Reactor at rest. Precedence when several apply: kill > offline > alert > attention > warming > speaking > listening > tool > thinking > goal (an overlay) > idle.

idle.$description: No turn, no goal, link up. Breathes.

listening.$description: Push-to-talk held or the wake word heard. The core follows the microphone.

thinking.$description: A prompt answered, no token yet. The middle ring's arc sweeps.

speaking.$description: TTS playing. The rings pulse on the envelope.

tool.$description: A tool running. One lit outer segment per active tool.

goal.$description: A goal active: a satellite dot orbits the outer ring, over whatever state is underneath.

attention.$description: An approval, a clarifying question, a parked goal. A held pulse.

warming.$description: The model cold-starting. Luminance ramps with progress.

alert.$description: An error while a turn runs, or a threshold alert. Three fast pulses, then hold.

kill.$description: The kill switch engaged: the one lit ring. The other rings are color.orb.housing; the room goes dark (no halo, neutral rims).

offline.$description: offline: brief §1 says the offline orb is desaturated with an amber ring and an OFFLINE label, never a silent idle.

paper.$description: The ground a QR code is printed on. Not a palette colour — a camera needs the contrast.

persona.$description: The two personas' hues (AURA, JARVIS). Either can be primary, so these are not 'a subagent's colour'. Ultron, Ada and Friday went at the owner's word (T-0936). Both clear 8:1 against the void.

aura.$description: AURA's hue: her theme's accent (themes/aura/theme.json, T-0861). Under her own theme it is the accent itself, so the reactor adds no tint.

jarvis.$description: An alias of the reactor's own light, so no hue is added for it. Named here because JARVIS is one of two switchable identities and not the permanent centre.

core-glow.$description: The radial glow behind the core (v2): the centre stop of the ground's radial gradient (chrome.stage-ground).

core.$description: The v2 core's own light (jarvis-web/src/lib/ds/core, ported from docs/design/v2/reference/orb_engine.js). The state hues are the base colours (accent, violet, danger); these are the whites and tints the engine mixes, so the WebGL and the Canvas2D renderer read one table.

haze.$description: The middle stop of the ground's radial gradient, between core-glow and bg.

speak.$description: The core's colour while speaking: the accent lifted toward white.

work.$description: The core's colour while working on a device.

hot.$description: The few hot particles in the shell (3 %): white sparks, never amber, which means waiting on a person (T-0749).

white.$description: The hottest light: the core's centre, the LEDs, the wire sphere, a segment edge at full light.

spark.$description: Light flowing along the rings, and the wire windings.

halo.$description: The core's glow between its white centre and the state colour.

face.$description: A ring segment's inner face: dark, so the faces turned away hide behind the lit edges.

violet.$description: Violet (brief §1): memory and embeddings — the memory globe, an embedding stream, a second data series (upload, a second model).

map.$description: The car's flat map (T-1252): a top-down street map in AURA's dark blue, drawn while the 3D drive is paused. The route and the car take the accent; a street's name takes text-bright. Map colours only: never for a control or a state.

land.$description: The ground where the map has nothing else.

water.$description: A lake, a river, the sea.

park.$description: A park, a wood, a field: anything green.

building.$description: A building's footprint, one step off the land.

casing.$description: The dark edge round a road and the halo behind a street's name.

road-minor.$description: A driveway, an aisle or a service road.

road-major.$description: A motorway, a trunk road or a primary road.

world.$description: The car map's real-world palette (T-1060): what the ground, the roads and the things beside them are drawn in when the map gives no colour of its own. Scene colours of a drawn place, not UI meaning: never for a control, a label or a state.

asphalt-minor.$description: A driveway's, an aisle's or a service road's surface.

path.$description: A footpath's or a cycle path's surface.

marking.$description: Painted road lines: edges, lane dashes, crossing stripes, parking bays.

wood.$description: Woodland on the ground, under its trees.

water.$description: A lake, a pond, a basin.

wall.$description: A building whose kind the map does not say.

wall-home.$description: A house, a flat block or anything lived in.

wall-trade.$description: A shop, an office, a hotel.

wall-works.$description: A factory, a warehouse, a garage, a shed.

wall-civic.$description: A school, a church, a hospital, a public building.

roof.$description: A flat roof with no colour given.

roof-home.$description: A pitched roof with no colour given.

glass.$description: A window, seen from the street by day.

canopy.$description: A tree's leaves in the light.

canopy-shade.$description: A tree's leaves in its own shade.

pole.$description: A lamp post or a signal pole.

lamp.$description: A street lamp's head, and at an alpha the pool of light under it.

signal.$description: A traffic signal's housing. Its three lenses are drawn in their own colours, unlit: nothing says which one is on.

signal-red.$description: A signal's top lens (T-1104): the red a signal is, not a state. Never the UI's danger.

signal-amber.$description: A signal's middle lens, the amber a signal is.

signal-green.$description: A signal's bottom lens, the green a signal is. Never the UI's ok.

ground.$description: Bare ground on the car's map, where nothing is mapped (T-1188): a muted olive-green, so tarmac reads against land and not against one flat grey. Lit by the day's light like everything else, so it is near-black at night.

field.$description: Farmland on the car's map (T-1188): a dry, tilled tone a little browner than bare ground.

yard.$description: Residential land on the car's map (T-1188): gardens and lawns between houses, a little greener than bare ground and duller than a park.

paved.$description: Commercial, retail and industrial land on the car's map (T-1188): yards, forecourts and slabs, a cool grey just under tarmac.

land.$description: Open ground on the car's map where the ground has height (T-1105): a slope facing away from the sun.

land-lit.$description: Open ground on a slope that faces the sun (T-1105); level ground is halfway between this and land.

pavement.$description: The pavement beside a town street on the car's ground (T-1104).

kerb.$description: The kerb stone between a street and its pavement.

barrier.$description: A guard rail, a concrete barrier or a bollard on the car's ground.

sign-blade.$description: A street-name sign's blade, the green the road uses for one.

sign-ink.$description: What a white sign says: a speed limit's number, a sign's words.

sign-stop.$description: A stop sign's octagon on the car's ground, the red the road uses.

sign-plate.$description: The white of a give-way triangle and a speed-limit plate.

fascia-food.$description: The sign board over a place that serves food or drink (T-1106): a cafe, a restaurant, a bakery, a bar.

fascia-shop.$description: The sign board over any other shop (T-1106).

fascia-service.$description: The sign board over a bank, a pharmacy, a clinic, an office or a place to stay (T-1106).

fascia-fuel.$description: The sign board over a filling station, a charging point or a garage (T-1106).

sky-day.$description: The top of the car map's sky in full day (T-1107); at night the sky is the ground colours it always was.

sky-day-horizon.$description: The day sky where it meets the land (T-1107).

sky-dusk.$description: The horizon while the sun is at it, rising or setting (T-1107).

window-lit.$description: A window with a light on behind it after dark (T-1107).

sign-warn.$description: Any other traffic sign: a warning diamond's yellow.

camera.$description: The housing of a surveillance camera or a plate reader on its pole.

camera-speed.$description: A speed camera's box, the yellow they are painted so a driver sees them.

camera-alpr.$description: The solar panel over a plate reader (a Flock camera), which tells it from any other camera.

haze.$description: What distance fades the world into.

chrome.$description: Data, timestamps, ids, code — the same face as the UI now (brief §1), named apart so a readout can still ask for mono by name. Self-hosted from jarvis-web/static/fonts.

body.$description: The UI face (brief §1): JetBrains Mono for everything a person reads, labels uppercase and tracked (type.tracking.label). Self-hosted at 400, 500 and 600; Android bundles the same files under res/font.

display.$description: Big numbers (brief §1): Space Grotesk Light (type.weight.display) for readout figures, the detail card's value, the wordmark. Self-hosted at 300 and 400.

size.$description: The console's scale in rem, for a mono face (brief §1: labels 10–11 px, the boards' running text 11.5–14 px). The floor is 0.6875rem (11 px at a 16 px root), the brief's upper label size; tokens.test.ts refuses anything smaller.

2xs.$description: Labels: the uppercase tracked captions (11 px).

xs.$description: Meta: timestamps, a row's second line, chips.

sm.$description: Dense running text: a row's title, a toast, a menu item.

md.$description: Running text: the reply, an input, a paragraph.

lg.$description: A figure in a row, a dialog's lead.

xl.$description: A small readout figure (Space Grotesk Light).

2xl.$description: The orbiting readouts' figures (the boards' 26 px).

display.$description: The detail card's value (the boards' 52 px).
The reply line and the big figure: light, so size carries the weight.

strong.$description: The one primary control per panel. Nothing else is set this heavy.

tracking.$description: The brief's labels are UPPERCASE and tracked .16–.2em (brief §1); running text stays at 0. A tracked word is always uppercase: tracked sentence case reads as spaced-out letters (the owner, 2026-09-24).

snug.$description: A hair of tracking on running text set in the display face, and on mono readouts (ids, timestamps, the status words).

label.$description: Uppercase labels (v2: .22em): section captions, rail entries, readout keys, the dock's captions.

control.$description: Uppercase control text: buttons, chips, toggles, status words.

android.$description: The phone's type scale in sp, named for the job. Pinned by android-app/tools/type_scale_test.py as a rename, not a redesign; change it here and there together.

relative.$description: Sizes relative to the text they sit in rather than to the root — a caret, a line. Not part of the type scale.

caret.$description: A caret, sized against the line it sits in rather than the root.

line.$description: One line of the surrounding text: the floor for a bubble that may still be empty.

space.$description: The console's rhythm in rem. 1–5 are the steps the chrome already uses; 6 and 7 are Reactor II's wide gutters.

micro.$description: Line spacing, and the inset on a 3 dp radius. Below this is a hairline.

step.$description: Between a row and the next thing that is not part of it.

sm.$description: Buttons, inputs, chips that are not pills (the boards' .btn).

md.$description: The panel grade (brief §1: 3 px): panels, cards, dialogs, popups (material.*.radius).

lg.$description: The dock and the rail's buttons.

glow-md.$description: The focused panel's glow, recoloured to the reactor's state colour; the reactor core; the push-to-talk ring.

glow-text.$description: v2: projected text is light, so every line of it carries this text-shadow.

glow-subtitle.$description: v2: the subtitles' wider glow, at the display size.

glow-bracket.$description: v2: the projection's one top-left bracket, glowing outward from its corner.

panel.$description: A panel tilted toward the core (the boards' tiltL/tiltR shadow): a dark drop below and a faint cyan halo.

float.$description: A popup, a toast, a dialog (the Popups board's .hud).

material.$description: Brief §1: every panel is the panel colour at 0.78 alpha under a 1 px cyan edge at 14 %, 3 px radius, with cyan corner brackets (chrome.bracket). No backdrop blur (DECISIONS.md #6). The three grades differ in fill, edge and radius.

pane.$description: Large background surfaces: the Focus rail, the Ambient strip, the phone's stack ground, a dialog's scrim. Carries Text and Muted only, never Faint (§5.4).

solid.$description: Reduced transparency, or past the blur budget: the same hierarchy with no blur (§5.3).

panel.$description: Every content panel. The title bar is part of the panel — same tint, a color.line-hair rule below it — not a second surface.

edge-hover.$description: A hovered or lifted panel's edge (the Ops board's .pane:hover).

refract.$description: The refraction hint's angle: on hover or drag the inner edge gradient turns this far toward the pointer over motion.dur.fast (§5.1). Nothing else at rest.

control.$description: Glass on glass: buttons, inputs, selects, chips, toggles, the drag and resize handles, dialogs, the command palette. A filled control (the one primary per panel, or a danger action) has no edge and carries Ink text.

edge.$description: 1 px, the boards' .btn border. A filled control has none.

solid.$description: An input's or a quiet control's fill.

floating.$description: The floating assistant, the island (T-0695): the desktop popup and the phone's overlay, over other apps, a pill at the top that grows into a card and back (tests/contracts/island.json). The one surface with a shaped edge and a blur behind it — the owner's asks (2026-10-07, 2026-11-09: 'something like a dynamic island'), an exception to ADR-0031 scoped to what floats over someone else's screen. Its backing is opaque, not frosted: what is behind never reads through the words.

fill.$description: The island's backing: dark enough for AA text over white or black content, blurred behind or not (overlay_scrim_test.py measures it).

radius.$description: Every corner of the island, pill or card: half of pill-height, so the pill is a capsule and the card keeps the same corners, and the morph between them is a change of bounds alone.

pill-height.$description: The pill's height: a touch target, since a tap opens it.

pill-width.$description: The pill with the core and its state word ('LISTENING', 'THINKING').

rest-width.$description: The resting island on the phone's camera while the assistant is on (T-0890): the persona and its state, or the time either side of the camera and the phone's status, with the hole between.

rest-height.$description: The resting island's height: about the status bar's, so it sits around the camera hole and not under it.

core-rest.$description: The core in the resting island's left end: the worn persona's own core (AURA's galaxy, the reactor) as one still frame, so it costs no frames at rest; inside the 32 px pill with a margin

activity-width.$description: The pill of an ongoing activity: its glyph, what it is (a destination) and its figure (the distance).

card-width.$description: The widest the island's card grows; narrower screens take their width less the gutters.

core-pill.$description: The core in the pill: one view with the card's, scaled down into the pill's slot, so it is the same Jarvis moving rather than a second one appearing.

core-card.$description: The core at the card's top left, beside its state word and what it is doing.

dim.$description: What lies over the screen behind the island while it has the focus (the card, an approval), with the blur; none behind the pill.

blur.$description: The blur behind the island while it has the focus (the phone's blur-behind radius, the desktop's backdrop-filter); none behind the pill.

halo.$description: How far the state-coloured glow reaches outside the card's edge.

glow.$description: The phone's reactor while it talks at the bottom (T-0912): the circle its soft glow fades out in, round the core alone, with no box and nothing dimmed past it.

orb.$description: The core alone at the bottom as an orb (T-0968, the owner: 'like an actual orb not just a circle'): the lit sphere inside the glow, the core within it.

orb-light.$description: The orb's specular highlight, top left, over the core: the glass catching the light.

orb-rim.$description: The orb's rim, where its edge catches the worn theme's light.

orb-shade.$description: The orb's unlit side, bottom right, and the soft shadow it casts below itself.

light.$description: The reactor's own core brightness per state, read by the web's reactor spec and the phone's. The rim, shadow and mix that lit panels from it are gone with the light layer (ADR-0031).

halo.$description: The ambient halo: a radial gradient centred on the reactor, rgba(C, k) to transparent over `extent`. k per state; speaking and warming move between their value and their peak (the TTS envelope, the cold-start progress).

spring.$description: The three springs (GLASS_HUD §8.1): interruptible — a retarget starts from the current position and velocity — never longer than settle, and transform/opacity only. Compose uses the same physics as spring(stiffness, dampingRatio); the ratio is damping / (2·√(stiffness·mass)), derived by build.py as spring.*.ratio so it cannot be typed apart from the numbers it comes from. The console has no springs: it plays settle at 30 fps on motion.ease.standard.

glass.$description: A panel opening, moving, resizing, changing mode; layout choreography; a timeline row drawing in.

snap.$description: A dragged panel docking into a tile slot or a snap line; drag release.

control.$description: Hover lift, a toggle, a chip, a handle appearing.

camera.$description: Every camera move on the map: flying to a panel, framing everything, returning to the reactor. Slower than a panel's spring because the move crosses the whole screen — a camera on spring.glass reads as thrown rather than flown (HUD.md §5).

base.$description: A tab indicator sliding, a panel opening.

enter.$description: A panel's entrance on first paint.

sweep.$description: An indeterminate bar crossing its track once.

blink.$description: A status dot's slow pulse — noticeable at the edge of vision, not distracting.

panel-summon.$description: A HUD panel arriving on the surface: scale 0.96→1, opacity 0→1 (tests/contracts/hud-panels.json motion.summon_ms).

panel-dismiss.$description: A HUD panel leaving: ease-in to 0.98 and 0 (hud-panels.json motion.dismiss_ms).

panel-reorder.$description: A HUD panel's neighbours closing the gap it left (hud-panels.json motion.reorder_ms).

panel-reduced.$description: prefers-reduced-motion: every panel move collapses to opacity-only at this length (hud-panels.json motion.reduced_motion_ms).

float-in.$description: The floating assistant arriving: rise, scale 0.94 to 1, fade, the blur coming in.

float-out.$description: The floating assistant leaving: quicker than it came, so a dismissal feels immediate.

glide.$description: A floating window moving to a new place on the screen, eased.

scan.$description: Section switch: the content is revealed top to bottom (the boards' scanIn).

unfold.$description: Bring up detail: a card unfolds from a line to full width to full height (the boards' unfold).

boot.$description: Boot: the side panels swing in from rotateY 55° to their 10° tilt (the boards' bootL/bootR).

appear.$description: v2: a projection comes out of the core (bright point, travel, thin line, full height).

exit.$description: v2: everything on stage leaves before the next scene comes out: projections collapse, lines retract, the strip folds, subtitles fade.

bar.$description: v2: a bar in a projected chart rising.

row-in.$description: v2: one row of a projection sliding in (motion.stagger.project apart).

connector.$description: v2: a connector or leader line drawing in from the core.

beat.$description: v2: the working beat: a pulse of light along each connector, and the core's kick while working.

shock.$description: v2: the shock ring every core state change fires, from the core out past the rings.

kick.$description: v2: the core's flash of extra glow on a state change.

fade.$description: v2: the subtitles fading in or out.

unroll.$description: v2: the presence strip unrolling from the core, or folding back.

hold.$description: v2: how long hold-to-confirm must be held (the Control board's ring).

undo.$description: v2: how long the shell offers Undo after a setting was changed (T-0700). A wait, not a movement: reduced motion does not shorten it.

out.$description: Brief §1: the one easing — everything that arrives or settles.

decelerate.$description: Something arriving: fast at the start, settling. Panels, sheets, anything entering.

accelerate.$description: Something leaving: slow to commit, then gone. Never for an entrance — it reads as a stutter.

spring.$description: Overshoot and settle, for a thing that should feel physical. Same curve as `overshoot`.

scan.$description: The scan-in reveal and its sweep line (the boards' scanIn/sweep).

appear.$description: v2: a projection coming out of the core (the Core2 board's mat).

exit.$description: v2: a projection collapsing back into the core (demat): slow to commit, then gone.

quick.$description: v2: a small projection that pops out rather than travels.

step.$description: The boot's per-panel step and a list's entrance step (GLASS_HUD's 40 ms ceiling).

row.$description: Section switch (BUILD_BRIEF §1): after the scan-in, rows slide in about 70 ms apart.

row-cap.$description: The eighth row starts here; anything later starts with it.

project.$description: v2: rows of a projection slide in this far apart.

boot.$description: The boot (GLASS_HUD §8.2, last row; §8.3 rule 5): the reactor ignites over motion.dur.enter, then each panel is traced in from its top-left corner (a clip that opens to the bottom-right) with the stagger above. The number the web and the phone would otherwise each type: the scale a panel settles FROM. There is no blur: the owner rejected the glass (ADR-0031) and the boot's entry blur was the last of it (2026-09-24).

scale.$description: A condensing panel starts this much larger than it settles.

reactor.$description: The reactor's own clock: rotation periods and the breath. Three speeds so the rings never phase-lock.

think.$description: The fine dashed ring inside the lens while the model is thinking: the one part of the instrument that turns fast enough to read as work.

speak.$description: The blades' cadence while Jarvis speaks: one beat per syllable-ish, so the instrument reads as talking rather than turning.

comet.$description: One lap of the comet that sweeps the coil while Jarvis thinks (2026-10-08): fast enough to read as work at a glance across a room, slow enough that its tail reads as a tail.

heartbeat.$description: The core's double beat while Jarvis thinks: two quick swells and a rest, so thinking has a pulse of its own and is not mistaken for idle breathing.

chase.$description: One lap of the light chasing round the bezel while a tool runs: the loading dial, so working is told apart from thinking.

ripple.$description: How long one ripple takes to travel from the core to the bezel while Jarvis speaks; three are in flight at once, a third apart.

beacon.$description: The rim's beacon while Jarvis needs you: a slow strong pulse with a halo leaving it, so attention reads from across a room.

strobe.$description: The alert's two flashes and a gap: urgent without becoming a seizure-rate flicker (under 3 Hz).

drift.$description: The 2D reactor's whole-body motion: a slow float at rest and a wider wander while it thinks (the owner, 2026-10-08: 'it moves around depending on what it is doing'). Slow, so the instrument breathes rather than bobs.

orbit.$description: One lap of the satellites that circle the 2D reactor while it acts (a tool running); each satellite runs a multiple of it so they never line up.

sweep.$description: One turn of the radar sweep inside the 2D reactor's core while it thinks.

tumble.$description: The base period for a ring to precess once about the axes across the view — the orb-only motion that makes the bands read as rings in space rather than discs turning in a plane. Each ring multiplies this by its own ratio and sign (geometry.ts TUMBLE), so no two precess at the same rate or in the same direction and the set never phase-locks. Slow on purpose: a tumble faster than the blades' spin reads as wobble.

ambient.$description: Ambient drift: rotations slow enough to read as alive rather than as motion.

budget.$description: What a choreography may cost. Measured by motion.spec.ts; a token so the number is one place.

frame.$description: The longest frame any choreography may take; over it the animation is doing layout, not drawing.

hover.$description: Hover intent on the map (HUD.md §5). A pointer sweeping across twenty glyphs must not set off twenty expansions, so a glyph becomes a card only after `in` of continuous hover and falls back only after `out` of no hover. Keyboard focus expands with no `in` delay — the person aimed — and collapses on the same `out`.

long-press.$description: Android's equivalent of hover intent: touch has no hover, so a long press is what asks a glyph to become a card.

stage-ground.$description: v2: the stage's ground: never flat, lit from the core outward (the Core2 board's background).

projection-backing.$description: v2: the dark radial behind projected text, so light reads over the core and its rings. Never a card: no edge, no fill to the corners.

projection-tint.$description: v2: the faint cyan bleed around a projection, the light it is made of spilling past its text.

projection-bleed.$description: v2: how far the backing and the tint reach past a projection's box.

projection-bracket.$description: v2: the arm of a projection's one top-left bracket.

projection-tilt.$description: v2: how far a projection turns toward the core once it stands at full height (rotateY, signed by the side it is on).

projection-perspective.$description: v2: the perspective a projection's tilt is seen under.

strip-width.$description: v2: the presence strip's width at most (it narrows to 40vw).

core-width.$description: v2: the core's stage at most (it narrows to 86vw).

rule-live.$description: The accent rule that marks the one row happening now: an inset box-shadow, not a border, so it does not move the layout.

measure-dialog.$description: How wide a modal question gets before it stops growing.

measure-panel.$description: How wide a screen or sheet is when it slides in beside the core (T-0725): a dialog's measure, never under 46% of the window nor over 62%, so the core always keeps a stage beside it.

measure-panel-rise.$description: How tall a screen or sheet is when it rises on a phone (T-0725): two thirds, so the core keeps the top third.

measure-wide.$description: How wide a screen of panels side by side gets (the Board's three columns): wider, each panel's drawing scales its labels past what a glance reads.

measure-orb.$description: The HUD orb stops growing here: bigger reads as a lava lamp, not an instrument.

measure-boot.$description: The boot sequence's stage — the same square the orb settles into.

measure-qr.$description: A pairing QR at the size a phone camera reads across a desk.

measure-log.$description: How tall a scrolling output pane gets before it stops growing and starts scrolling.

measure-panel-min.$description: The narrowest a tiled panel is drawn. A row split whose two children would each be narrower than this renders as a column instead (jarvis-web rects.ts), so the Working preset's goal and model stack under the turn beside the stage rather than sharing a column at half this, and a narrow window stacks what a wide one puts side by side. The document is untouched: it is how the split is drawn, not what it says.

measure-card.$description: A connection card's width. The orb's placement solver is told this same number, and `place()` keeps boxes apart on the numbers it is given — a card that renders wider than it was declared lands on its neighbours. Typed once so the CSS and the solver cannot disagree.

measure-card-height.$description: A connection card's height, exact rather than a minimum. The orb's solver is told this number and keeps boxes apart on it, so the rendered card has to be it: as a min-height the content came out 105 and the told size was fiction again, in miniature. Content past it is clipped, which is what 'a card is a glance' means.

measure-token-perspective.$description: The perspective a map token's cube turns under (HUD.md §6.1, PanelToken). Far on purpose: the near corner of a glyph's cube grows by under two per cent at any turn, which is the allowance `CUBE_FIT` leaves inside the slot the overlap gate measured, and a card's face by under a pixel.

measure-token-depth.$description: How thick a map card is (HUD.md §6.1). A glyph is a true cube, as deep as it is wide, so it has a flank to show as the room turns; a card is a reading surface that faces the camera, and this is the slab under it -- enough for an edge and a top, not a block behind two lines of text.

bracket.$description: The corner brackets' arm length (brief §1): top-left and bottom-right of every panel, in color.accent.

tilt.$description: How far a side panel turns toward the core at rest (brief §1, the boards' rotateY(±10deg)).

tilt-boot.$description: Where a side panel starts its boot swing.

perspective.$description: The perspective the side panels and the dock are tilted in.

rail-closed.$description: The left rail collapsed to icons.

size.$description: Android control and ornament sizes in dp (JarvisUi.Size). A size is not a gap: these are how big a THING is, and snapping them to the spacing scale is how a 34 dp button becomes a 32 dp one nobody meant.

chip.$description: A spacer between two buttons, and the smallest tap ornament.

inset.$description: The inset of a sheet's own padding from the screen's.

edge.$description: The consent button's corner radius — a pill on a 52 dp control.

sheet.$description: The margin a sheet keeps from the screen edge.

wide_button.$description: The side padding of a consent button, which is deliberately wider than any other control in the app: it is the one nobody may press by accident.

drop.$description: How far below the top edge a floating panel sits.

panel_max.$description: The widest a floating panel gets, whatever the screen.

sheet_min.$description: The shortest a sheet gets before it scrolls.

touch.$description: The smallest a control a finger lands on may be, in either direction (GLASS_HUD §12; Android's own touch-target bar, the one ATF's TouchTargetSizeCheck measures). A View control's minHeight/minWidth, not its padding: the visible box may stay smaller.

car_mark.$description: The car screen's app mark and the icon on a car tile (ADR-0047): big enough to find at a glance on an 800x480 head unit, scaled by the car's density like every car size.

car_art.$description: Album art on the car's now-playing tile (ADR-0047).

car_art_small.$description: Album art on a row of the car's music library and queue (ADR-0047).

car_touch.$description: The smallest target on the hologram drive (T-0613, Car.dc.html): a drawn button and an icon button, at arm's length in a moving car.

car_margin.$description: The drive's side margin: the turn, trip and subtitle zones sit this far in from the visible area (Car.dc.html).

car_top.$description: How far below the visible area's top the turn and trip zones sit.

car_bottom.$description: How far above the visible area's bottom the subtitle zone sits.

car_core.$description: The core on the drive, bottom right.

car_core_right.$description: The core's inset from the visible area's right edge.

car_core_bottom.$description: The core's inset from the visible area's bottom edge.

car_card.$description: The widest the drive's one contextual card gets.

car_card_gap.$description: The gap between the card and the core, and between any two zones.

car_subtitle.$description: The widest the subtitle zone (what Jarvis says) gets.

car_turn_icon.$description: The next turn's arrow, top left.

car_text_turn.$description: The next turn's distance: the one number a driver reads at a glance. Car text is sized against the car's density, not the phone's font scale, so it lives here rather than in type.

car_text_speed.$description: The speed, under the trip line.

car_text_title.$description: A card's title (who is calling, the song).

car_text_line.$description: What Jarvis says, and a card's longer body.

car_label_min.$description: The smallest a street label on the drive is drawn, however far away: below this it is not readable at a glance and is faded out instead.

car_label_max.$description: The largest a street label on the drive is drawn, however close.

emission.$description: The three emission grades (HUD.md §4). A panel is light projected into space, so its presence is an alpha over the void plus a luminous contour, never a fill plus a shadow. Field is the substrate the bands are drawn on, Panel is a panel body, Control is anything that answers a pointer. Bloom is budgeted: only the reactor and the one focused panel bloom noticeably, because a bloom pass on everything is a blur pass.

field.$description: Bands, the substrate, the halo, any large background surface.

surface.$description: A pane behind panels: the ground one step up, translucent.

contour-focus.$description: The focused or hovered panel's edge (the boards' selected rail button, .pane:hover).

bloom.$description: Alpha of the panel's `0 0 18px accent` bloom. The cap for anything that is not the reactor or the focused panel.

control.$description: Buttons, inputs, chips, the composer — anything that answers a pointer immediately.

band.$description: The three orbital bands (HUD.md §6.1). `radius` is in scene units with the reactor at the origin; `falloff` is the atmospheric opacity multiplier applied to everything on that band, which is how distance reads without a shadow. `gutter` is the minimum angular gap between two panels on the inner band; the solver scales it by radius so the gap is a constant number of pixels on every band.

min-legible.$description:
The floor the atmospheric falloff is clamped to when it is applied as a composite opacity.

Falloff is meant to dim a band's *emission* — its surface and its contour — and not the type on it. Applied to the whole panel it dims the type as well: axe measured a house heading at 4.24:1 against a 4.5 threshold, because #7c9ea9 at the middle band's 0.75 composites to #5e7882. Until the surface and the contour can carry the falloff on their own, the composite is floored here and an open panel — the thing being read — takes none of it (HUD.md §3, §4).

crew-gap.$description: How far outside the outer band a companion sphere sits (JARVIS_SCENE_BRIEF PART 3: a subagent's reactor lives outside the panels). In pixels, not scene units, so a companion arriving does not refit the room: the panels' rings stay put and the crew hang beyond them.

camera.$description: The camera's bounds and density thresholds (HUD.md §6.4). Pitch is bounded and roll does not exist because a camera that can tumble has no 'back'; `glyph-below` and `open-above` are the zoom levels at which density changes, which is what makes zooming out a way to see the whole system rather than a smaller picture of part of it.

glyph-below.$description: Below this zoom every panel draws as a glyph.

open-above.$description: Above this zoom a card draws as an open panel.

parallax.$description: Fraction of the viewport the scene orbits on pointer movement. Small on purpose: the room should breathe, not swing.

sound.$description: The console's earcons, synthesised with WebAudio (no audio asset). `ack` plays the instant a prompt is submitted while replies are spoken, so the ~1.3 s before the first spoken word is not silence: two soft rising sine notes, quiet enough to sit under a voice.

high.$description: Hz, the second note: a fourth up, which reads as 'heard' rather than as an alert.

gain.$description: Peak gain, 0-1; a spoken reply plays at 1.

note.$description: Each note's length, attack and release included.
